data.title: Permission Mode
data.tagline: A set of control presets defining file system boundaries, network access limits, and user confirmation triggers for an AI agent.
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish Codex's Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access, and Custom settings, then choose settings for read-only analysis, routine changes, and wider access.
data.description: For example, one Codex permission option can allow routine reads, writes, and local commands inside the current workspace, then ask before network access or crossing that boundary. Names and combinations differ across tools. Check the sandbox scope, when prompts appear, and who reviews them before choosing.

learning.assumes: You know that an AI agent may read files, edit code, or run terminal commands.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish Codex's Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access, and Custom settings, then choose settings for read-only analysis, routine changes, and wider access.

distinctions.label: Sandbox
distinctions.explanation: A Sandbox is a runtime isolation barrier enforced by the operating system or container; a Permission Mode defines user confirmation rules and operational freedom for an AI tool.

data.boundary: The sandbox determines which files, networks, and system resources commands can access; the approval policy determines when an action pauses to ask. A product may combine both into one permission option, but approving an action does not automatically widen the sandbox, and fewer prompts do not mean there is no access boundary.

lessonPractice.title: Which statement about permission modes is correct?

options.label: Plan / read-only is mainly for reading and analysis without changing code; after confirming the plan, move to the execution phase
options.feedback: Correct. Plan / read-only is for understanding context and preparing a plan. Code changes should happen after confirmation, with access and approval settings chosen for the task.

options.label: Full access only changes model capability and does not affect the AI's access to files or network resources
options.feedback: Not quite. Full access widens or removes sandbox restrictions, which affects the files and network resources the AI can access.

options.label: Ask for approval means the AI can never change code and may only ask the user questions
options.feedback: Not quite. Ask for approval means the AI asks before actions that need approval. After approval, it may still change code within the permitted scope.

data.agentPrompt: Before any code development, first confirm the requirements with me, read the necessary context in Plan or read-only mode, and prepare a clear approach and plan. Do not change code or perform other development actions until I confirm the plan. After confirmation, choose the permission settings that match the task's access scope; explain the impact before widening the scope, then inspect the Diff and run the tests.
